candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.7, Management of Care — Legal Rights and Responsibilities; Concepts of Management
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — employment-related grievance process under a collective-bargaining agreement
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that a union-represented employee challenging a matter covered by a collective-bargaining agreement should use the agreement-specific grievance process rather than assume universal rules or bypass the negotiated procedure.

options.A: Discuss the issue only informally with coworkers because negotiated grievance procedures should not be used for covered disciplinary disputes.
options.B: Assume the same grievance steps and deadlines apply in every workplace, regardless of the collective-bargaining agreement.
options.C: Review and use the grievance procedure provided by the applicable collective-bargaining agreement, following any specified steps and time limits and seeking union representation or assistance as appropriate.
options.D: Resign immediately because disciplinary actions covered by a collective-bargaining agreement cannot be reviewed through a grievance process.

candidate.rationale: The National Labor Relations Act recognizes employee grievances and treats final adjustment by a method agreed on by the parties as the desirable method for resolving disputes arising from the application or interpretation of an existing collective-bargaining agreement. The NLRB also recognizes a union's duty of fair representation when handling grievances. Because procedures differ by agreement, the nurse should use the applicable negotiated process and follow its actual requirements rather than assume a universal procedure. C is therefore the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Federal labor law recognizes grievances and negotiated dispute-resolution methods under collective-bargaining agreements; unions have a duty of fair representation when handling grievances, while specific procedures depend on the applicable agreement.
candidate.source_document_title: National Labor Relations Act; Right to fair representation
candidate.source_locator: NLRA Section 9(a) — employee grievances and bargaining representative; Section 203(d) — final adjustment by a method agreed upon by the parties for grievance disputes arising under an existing collective-bargaining agreement; NLRB Right to fair representation — handling grievances
candidate.source_version_date: Current federal statutory text and NLRB guidance; accessed 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: A union-represented nurse wants to challenge a disciplinary action that is covered by the nurse's collective-bargaining agreement. Which approach is most appropriate?
